question: Should the Lower-third tag on the captions wear the mock's four-diamond icon?
context: The captions mock puts a small violet Lower-third tag with the component icon on the top left of the lower third plate. The app already uses a violet chip with that icon on the canvas to mean this is a component. The tag is built and shipping without the icon until you choose.

options.label: Diamond icon, as the mock
options.summary: The tag reads Lower-third with the four-diamond icon in front, exactly as the captions mock draws it.
pros: Matches the mock to the pixel
cons: That violet chip with the four diamonds is the same chip the canvas puts on every component, so it tells people their captions are a component they can edit as one, which they are not
options.mitigation: Only shows while the timeline is open and the Lower third style is picked, so it is rare next to a real component.

options.label: Label only, as built now
options.summary: The tag reads Lower-third on the violet chip with no icon. This is what the app shows today.
pros: Says exactly what the style is and nothing more
Never mistaken for a component chip
cons: One step away from the mock: no icon
options.mitigation: The tag keeps the mock spot, colour, size and words.

options.label: Captions icon instead
options.summary: The tag reads Lower-third with the small speech-bubble captions icon the Words track already wears.
pros: The icon says captions, which is true
cons: One more icon on a small tag
options.mitigation: Uses the icon the captions track already shows, so nothing new to learn.

options.label: No tag at all
options.summary: Take the tag away. The violet plate low on the left is the only sign of the style.
options.mitigation: The style stays named in the Caption style tiles in the panel.

withdrawn.reason: reopened with option d no longer retiring the task: the tag is already built, so no tag means removing it
